chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I heard him saying: Any woman who is divorced, then her husband dies before her waiting period (iddah) expires and she has not become fully divorced (haram) to him, then she inherits him and then observes the waiting period of the one who died for her (the deceased husband). And if she dies while in her waiting period and has not become fully divorced to him, then he inherits her. And if he is killed, she inherits from his blood money (diyah), and if she is killed, he inherits from her blood money, provided that one did not kill the other.

key_terms.مَا لَمْ يَقْتُلْ أَحَدُهُمَا الْآخَرَ: Provided that one did not kill the other

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and iddah rules for a divorced woman if her husband dies before the divorce becomes final?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the legal status of a woman in the intermediate stage of triple divorce (talaq raj'i), where she is still considered a wife for inheritance purposes until the iddah expires. It establishes that she inherits from her husband and observes the widow's waiting period, while also detailing reciprocal rights to blood money (diyah) upon death, provided the death was not caused by the other party. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the finality of divorce is contingent upon the completion of the waiting period, preserving marital ties for financial and ritual obligations.
